title: Actual integral finite-quotient augmentation and perfect coefficient realization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and a chosen uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For any scheme $T$, use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and put $R_T=p_T^*\underline A$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For $j\geq1$ let $S_{j,T}=(A/\pi^j)_T$ be the constant finite ring sheaf, with the actual projection $q_{j,T}:R_T\to S_{j,T}$ obtained by pulling back the condensed continuous quotient map [def-sfb-integral-quotient-coefficients]. Use internal module objects and their ordinary unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], flat modules and K-flat complexes [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex].

The ring $A$ is commutative Noetherian, $\pi^j\ne0$, and every $A/\pi^j$ is finite and has the finite free $A$-resolution $[A\xrightarrow{\pi^j}A]$ in degrees $-1,0$. There is a canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism $R_T\cong\varprojlim_{j\geq1}S_{j,T}$ identifying every finite projection with $q_{j,T}$. The sheaf $R_T$ is flat over the constant sheaf $\underline A_T$, and multiplication by $\pi^j$ on $R_T$ is injective. The actual map $q_{j,T}$ induces $R_T/\pi^jR_T\cong S_{j,T}$. The complex $C_{j,T}=[R_T\xrightarrow{\pi^j}R_T]$, in degrees $-1,0$, has flat terms and is K-flat; its augmentation $C_{j,T}\to\operatorname{Res}_{q_{j,T}}S_{j,T}[0]$ with degree-zero component exactly $q_{j,T}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. These statements hold internally and under the fixed internal/section module equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence].

proof.text: Use the recorded DVR structure to obtain the principal-ideal-ring instance and apply Mathlib Noetherianity of a PID. The chosen uniformizer generates the nonzero maximal ideal, so it and all its positive powers are nonzero. Use the finite coefficient-quotient theorem. Domain cancellation proves injectivity, and Ideal.span_singleton_pow and Ideal.mem_span_singleton identify the kernel of the actual quotient map with the image of multiplication; quotient surjectivity completes the arithmetic exact sequence.

Construct the short exact sequence first on continuous condensed coefficients. On each profinite test space, nonzero-scalar cancellation gives injectivity; a set-theoretic lift from the discrete finite quotient is continuous and gives surjectivity. Continuous uniformizer division identifies the kernel with the image. The sectionwise exactness and point-pullback finite-limit helpers from the proved derived-Nakayama module transfer this short exact sequence to the actual pulled-back maps. Reflect along the faithful exact internal-module forgetful functor. Thus the specified projection, rather than an abstract quotient isomorphism, is the cokernel of the specified multiplication.

Apply the integral coefficient-limit theorem with its profinite normalization. Use the section-ring reconstruction helpers from the normalized-restriction-square module to lift its monoidal comparison to a commutative ring-sheaf isomorphism. Check the actual reduction map on the point-adjunction unit and use the theorem's normalization of every profinite quotient. Normalized finite-discrete encodings identify the finite section ring with the ordinary constant ring. Faithfulness of forgetting commutative ring structure proves the required projection square. Forget commutativity and invert the finite comparison to obtain exactly alpha and c in the statement.

Let I be the ideal generated by the lifted uniformizer in ULift A. The explicit quotient equivalence ULift A/I^(n+1) = ULift(A/(pi^(n+1))) intertwines the transition homomorphisms. It gives an isomorphism of the adic constant tower with the actual finite coefficient tower and hence of their limits, commuting with projections. The constant map has the canonical finite composites. Apply flat_presented_completion from the completed-constant-algebra theorem, using Noetherianity transported to ULift A. The fixed section equivalence carries the internal regular module to the unit section module; transport site-flatness along that isomorphism.

The cone of the degree-zero multiplication has one regular module in degree -1, one in degree 0, and zero terms elsewhere, by the standard cone biproduct decomposition. Unit flatness and these identifications make every term flat. The same support gives strict bounds [-1,0]. Apply the proved source bounded-flat K-flat criterion internally. The internal/section tensor comparison gives site-flatness of the section terms, and the independent-universe bounded-above flat criterion gives their K-flatness.

Apply the degree-zero single functor to the short exact sequence of step 2. Mathlib mappingCone.descShortComplex is the augmentation, mappingCone.inr_descShortComplex gives its composite with the unshifted inclusion exactly equal to the given quotient map, and mappingCone.quasiIso_descShortComplex proves it is a quasi-isomorphism. The exact section equivalence preserves homology, hence preserves this quasi-isomorphism. This proves every assertion about the original cone and actual augmentation in the ordinary unbounded categories.
